bullets.title: Semiconductors surge 10%+ in August, best month since 2003; DRAM revenue poised for historic leap
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks are up more than 10% this month, on track for their best August since 2003, with Korean chipmakers also surging on renewed AI demand. DRAM industry—which generated ~$1T cumulatively over 2010–2025—is now projected to generate $1T in a single year in 2027, a structural step-change in the memory market.

bullets.title: Memory bottleneck persists; SNDK notches 27% gain in one week
bullets.body: Fintwit notes the memory bottleneck across SNDK, MU, and Samsung remains structurally unresolved despite recent industry chatter. One trader flagged buying SNDK at $1,213 and selling at $1,544 for a 27% gain in a single week.

bullets.title: AMAT: strong quarter sold off; Street modeling issues flagged
bullets.body: Applied Materials posted a strong quarterly result but the market sold off the stock. A fintwit analyst flagged unclear Street modeling dynamics as the key issue to watch, with the $424B market cap name remaining one of the largest in semis.

bullets.title: Apple rolling out on-device GenAI in China via rare US-China partnership
bullets.body: Apple is preparing to launch its on-device generative AI service in China amid a rare US-China cooperative arrangement. The move is seen as a meaningful step for Apple's AI rollout in one of its largest markets.

bullets.title: Trump drone tariff proclamation more complex than headlines suggest; 100% tariffs on UAS components
bullets.body: Trump signed a drone proclamation imposing 100% tariffs on UAS docking stations and certain critical components (including vehicles >25kg), with the Secretary of Commerce gaining new discretionary authority. Fintwit cautions the structure is being 'treated wrong'—it's more nuanced than a simple headline tariff rate, and could broadly benefit US drone component suppliers.

bullets.title: Sanders threatens Congressional action to pause AI development
bullets.body: Senator Bernie Sanders called for a voluntary pause on AI development, threatening Congressional intervention if the industry does not comply. The statement adds regulatory overhang risk to AI-exposed names.

bullets.title: SPY at all-time highs; 8 of 11 sectors green on quad shift
bullets.body: 8 of 11 S&P sectors are trading in the green, driving SPY to an all-time high in what one macro framework describes as a textbook 'Quad Shift' pattern in August. S&P 500 profit margins are also reported at their highest level ever recorded.

bullets.title: Real-time card data points to large retail sales miss today
bullets.body: At least one macro account flagged that real-time credit/debit card spending data indicates weakness heading into the retail sales print, suggesting a significant downside miss versus consensus expectations.

bullets.title: VIX term structure steep; short-dated vol crushed pre-FOMC, longer-dated holds bid
bullets.body: The VIX term structure is notably steep as short-dated volatility heading into FOMC has been 'smashed lower,' while longer-dated vol (+3 months) remains bid. VIX expiration next week could free up vol, with potential for normalization. Meanwhile CBOE DSPX (dispersion index) is declining sharply as AI FOMO fades and crowded bull trades deleverage—software and financials are still outperforming.

bullets.title: US financial conditions at most accommodative since 1990s; yield curve at cycle high +51bps
bullets.body: Bloomberg's US Financial Conditions index has loosened to its most accommodative level since the 1990s, tracking money market, corporate, and muni spreads alongside equity valuations and implied vol. The 10s2s yield curve simultaneously steepened to a new cycle high of +51bps, with at least one macro fund positioned long steepeners.

bullets.title: September Fed rate hike probability falls below 33%
bullets.body: Markets are now pricing less than a 33% probability of a September Fed rate hike, reflecting softening in forward guidance expectations amid the current macro backdrop.

bullets.title: PBOC makes historic mid-month liquidity injection of $52B
bullets.body: The People's Bank of China injected 348 billion yuan (~$52 billion) into the banking system via overnight reverse repos in what is being flagged as the first mid-month injection of this kind in PBOC history, suggesting deliberate stimulus intent.

bullets.title: China credit growth misses; Jan-July new yuan loans CNY10.38T vs CNY10.62T estimate
bullets.body: China's January–July new yuan loan total came in at CNY10.38T, below the CNY10.62T consensus estimate, signaling weaker-than-expected credit demand despite the PBOC's liquidity operations.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz escalation: IRGC drones oil tanker; Saudi fleet going dark
bullets.body: IRGC struck an oil tanker with a drone after it attempted passage through the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian authorization. Separately, Saudi oil tankers are increasingly going 'dark' (disabling tracking) due to Houthi threats in the Red Sea. Brent crude rose 0.7% to $88/bbl with the US threatening an indefinite Iran naval blockade.

bullets.title: Taiwan on pace for first double-digit GDP growth since 2010
bullets.body: Taiwan is tracking double-digit GDP growth for the first time since 2010, a positive macro backdrop for the island's semiconductor and tech supply chain.

bullets.title: Goldman raises STOXX 600 target to 695 from 660; FTSE 100 to 11,400
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs increased its 12-month STOXX 600 target to 695 from 660 and raised its FTSE 100 forecast for next year to 11,400, reflecting improved European equity outlook.

bullets.title: Intel Razor Lake-AX revives cancelled Nova Lake-AX; MSI handheld partnership previewed
bullets.body: Intel's Razor Lake-AX resurrects the previously cancelled Nova Lake-AX architecture while Razor Lake-S skips a full generation ahead. Intel is also partnering with MSI on a handheld gaming device, described as a 'potato-free portable future,' signaling ambitions in portable computing.

bullets.title: Diesel crack spread hits all-time high; copper supply crunch deepens
bullets.body: Diesel crack spreads reached a new all-time high. Separately, LME copper spot prices are trading $260+ premium to October futures as inventories decline, with the September contract backwardation signaling acute near-term supply constraints.

bullets.title: Macro accounts net long Asian equities and bullish Nikkei; long yen
bullets.body: At least one macro fund has moved back to net long Asian equities and FX, with KOSPI flipping to a bullish trade signal and Nikkei/yen longs reiterated. US stocks characterized as remaining in the 'Investable Bucket' (bullish volatility regime).
